title: Homily II — The apostles gather like eagles

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily II on the Dormition, col. 732 (PDF leaf 407)

source_text: Τίνα δὲ τὰ ἐπ' αὐτῇ γέρα τότε τελούμενα πρὸς τοῦ γεραίρειν τοὺς τεκόντας θεσμοθετήσαντος; Τοὺς μὲν ἁπανταχοῦ τῆς γῆς πρὸς ἀνθρώπων ἁλείαν διασπαρέντας ταῖς πολυαρμονίαις καὶ ποικίλαις γλώσσαις τοῦ Πνεύματος, καὶ τῇ τοῦ λόγου σαγήνῃ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ζωγροῦντας ἐκ τοῦ τῆς πλάνης βυθοῦ πρὸς τὴν πνευματικὴν καὶ ἐπουράνιον τράπεζαν τοῦ δείπνου τοῦ μυστικοῦ τῆς ἱερᾶς πανδαισίας τῶν πνευματικῶν τοῦ οὐρανίου νυμφίου γάμων, οὓς ὁ Πατὴρ τῷ ἰσοσθενεῖ καὶ ὁμοφυεῖ Υἱῷ λαμπρῶς ἑστιᾷ, καὶ λίαν βασιλικώτατα θεῖον πρόσταγμα πρὸς Ἱερουσαλὴμ, ὥσπερ τις σαγήνη ἢ νεφέλη κατήπειγεν, ἐκ τῶν τερμάτων τῆς γῆς οἷά τινας ἀετοὺς συνωθοῦσα καὶ συναθροίζουσα. Ὅπου γὰρ τὸ πτῶμα, Χριστὸς ἡ ἀλήθεια ἔφησε, τοὺς ἀετοὺς συναχθήσεσθαι. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ περὶ τῆς αὐτοῦ τοῦ ταῦτα λέξαντος δευτέρας μεγάλης καὶ ἐπιφανοῦς παρουσίας, καὶ οὐρανόθεν καταφοιτήσεως, ἡ ῥῆσις ἥδε προλέλεκται, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἀτόπως ὥσπερ ἡδύσματι τοῦ λόγου κἀνταῦθα παραληφθήσεται. Παρῆσαν τοίνυν οἱ αὐτόπται καὶ τοῦ λόγου θεράποντες, κατ' ὀφειλὴν καὶ τῇ τούτου μητρὶ λειτουργήσοντες, καὶ κλῆρον ὥσπερ τινὰ πολυτελῆ καὶ ὑπέρτιμον τὴν εὐλογίαν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἀρυσόμενοι. Τίνι γάρ ἐστιν ἡ γνώμη ἀμφίβολος, ὡς αὕτη τῆς εὐλογίας πηγὴ καὶ πάντων τῶν ἀγαθῶν ὑπάρχει ἀνάβλυσις; Συμπαρῆσαν δὲ καὶ οἱ τούτων ὀπαδοὶ καὶ διάδοχοι, τῆς λειτουργίας ἅμα καὶ τῆς εὐλογίας μεθέξοντες. Ὧν γὰρ κοινὸς ὁ πόνος, καὶ αἱ ἐπικαρπίαι κατάλληλοι. Παρειστήκει δὲ καὶ τῶν ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ ὅσον θεόλεκτον σύστημα. Ἐχρῆν δὲ καὶ τῶν πάλαι δικαίων καὶ προφητῶν τοὺς ἀκρέμονας συμπαρομαρτεῖν, ταύτης τῆς ἱερᾶς δορυφορίας μεθέξοντας, τοὺς προκατηγγελκότας δηλαδὴ τὴν ἐξ αὐτῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγου δι' ἡμᾶς ἔνσαρκόν τε καὶ φιλάνθρωπον γέννησιν. Ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ἀγγέλων ὁμήγυρις ἄμοιρος. Ὅσον γὰρ τῷ βασιλεῖ κατὰ γνώμην ὑπήκουον, κἀντεῦθεν τῆς αὐτοῦ τιμαλφοῦς παραστάσεως ἄξιον, ἔδει δορυφορεῖν τὴν τούτου κατὰ σάρκα Μητέρα, τὴν πανολβίαν ὄντως καὶ μάκαρα, τὴν πασῶν γενεῶν καὶ κτίσεως ἁπάσης προφερεστέραν. Ταύτῃ παρειστήκεισαν ἅπαντες, τῇ φρυκτωρίᾳ λαμπομένῃ τοῦ Πνεύματος, καὶ τοῖς ἐκλάμπροις μαρμαρυγαῖς καταλαμπούσῃ τοὺς αἰδοῖ τε, καὶ φόβῳ, καὶ ἀκλινεῖ τῷ πόθῳ εἰλικρινὲς αὐτῇ ὄμμα νοητὸν ἐνερείδοντας. Ἔστι γὰρ τῶν ὄντων οὐδὲν, ὃ μὴ τοῦτο πέφυκεν, ἢ τὸ μόνον ἕν· ὅτι μηδὲν τῶν ὄντων τῷ ὑπερεῖναι, καὶ πρὸς οὐδὲν παρατιθέμενον κάτεισι, καὶ κατιόν γε πρὸς ἅπαντα, καὶ ποιοῦν, καὶ μὴ τὸ δρᾶσθαι δεχόμενον.
pass_a_gloss: What [were] the honours (γέρα) then paid (τελέω) to her by the one who legislated to honour (γεραίρω) the parents? Those scattered (διασπείρω) everywhere on earth for the fishing (ἁλεία) of men by the many-harmonied and varied (ποικίλος) tongues (γλῶσσαι) of the Spirit, and with the dragnet (σαγήνη) of the word catching alive (ζωγρέω) men out of the deep (βυθός) of error (πλάνη), to the spiritual and heavenly table (τράπεζα) of the mystical supper of the sacred feast (πανδαισία) of the spiritual marriage (γάμοι) of the heavenly bridegroom (νυμφίος), which the Father splendidly feasts (ἑστιάω) for the equal-in-strength (ἰσοσθενής) and same-natured (ὁμοφυής) Son, and very most royally — [them] a divine command (πρόσταγμα), like a dragnet or cloud (νεφέλη), urged (κατεπείγω) to Jerusalem, pushing together (συνωθέω) and gathering them like eagles (ἀετοί) from the ends (τέρματα) of the earth. For where the carcass/body (πτῶμα) [is], Christ the truth said, the eagles will be gathered (συνάγω). For even if this saying (ῥῆσις) was foretold about the second, great and manifest (ἐπιφανής) coming (παρουσία) of the very one who said it, and descent from heaven, yet not out of place as a seasoning (ἥδυσμα) of the discourse it will be taken up here too. Present then were the eyewitnesses (αὐτόπται) and servants of the word, as debt to serve also his mother, and to draw (ἀρύω) from her the blessing (εὐλογία) as a costly and more-than-precious inheritance (κλῆρος). To whom is the judgement (γνώμη) doubtful (ἀμφίβολος) that she is the spring (πηγή) of blessing and the welling-up (ἀνάβλυσις) of all goods? Present together also their followers (ὀπαδοί) and successors (διάδοχοι), to share (μετέχω) both the service and the blessing. For of whom the toil (πόνος) is common, the fruits also correspond. There stood by also whatever God-chosen (θεόλεκτος) company (σύστημα) of those in Jerusalem. It was fitting also that the topmost branches (ἀκρέμονες) of the righteous and prophets of old attend together, to share this sacred escort (δορυφορία), those namely who had announced beforehand the enfleshed (ἔνσαρκος) and man-loving birth (γέννησις) of God the Word from her for us. But neither [was] the gathering (ὁμήγυρις) of angels without share (ἄμοιρος). For as many as obeyed (ὑπακούω) the King by will, and hence [were] worthy of his precious standing-by, had to escort (δορυφορέω) his Mother according to flesh, the truly all-blessed (πανόλβιος) and happy (μάκαρ), more excellent than all generations and all creation. By her all stood, [her] shining (λάμπομαι) with the beacon-fire (φρυκτωρία) of the Spirit and with bright flashings illumining (καταλάμπω) those who with reverence (αἰδώς), fear and unswerving (ἀκλινής) longing fix (ἐνερείδω) on her a pure (εἰλικρινής) intellectual (νοητός) eye. For there is nothing of beings (τὰ ὄντα) which is not by nature (πέφυκε) this, or [except] the only One; because [it is] none of beings by being-beyond, and set beside (παρατίθημι) nothing it descends (κάτειμι), and descending indeed to all, both acting (ποιέω) and not receiving (δέχομαι) being acted upon (δρᾶσθαι).
pass_b_english: And what honours were paid to her then by the One who made it law to honour parents (Exodus 20:12)? There were those who had been scattered over all the earth to fish for men (Matthew 4:19) through the many-voiced and varied tongues of the Spirit, and who with the net of the word were catching men alive (Luke 5:10) out of the depth of error, for the spiritual and heavenly table of the mystical supper, the sacred banquet of the spiritual wedding of the heavenly Bridegroom, which the Father gives, splendidly and most royally, for the Son who is equal to him in power and one with him in nature (Matthew 22:2): these a divine command drove toward Jerusalem, like a net or a cloud, pressing and gathering them like eagles from the ends of the earth. For 'where the body is,' said Christ the Truth, 'there the eagles will be gathered' (Matthew 24:28). For although this saying was spoken beforehand about the second, great and glorious coming of the very One who said it, and his descent from heaven, it will not be out of place to take it up here too, as a seasoning for the discourse. So there were present the eyewitnesses and servants of the Word (Luke 1:2), to serve his mother as well, as was their duty, and to draw from her the blessing as a costly and priceless inheritance. For whose mind is in doubt that she is the spring of blessing and the source from which all good things well up? With them were present their followers and successors too, to share both the service and the blessing; for those who share the labour share alike in the fruits. And there stood by as well the whole company of God's chosen in Jerusalem. It was fitting, too, that the foremost of the righteous and the prophets of old should attend and share in this sacred escort, those, that is, who had foretold that God the Word would be born from her in the flesh, for our sake and in his love for mankind. Nor was the assembly of the angels left without a share. For all of them who obeyed the King of their own will, and so were worthy to stand in his honoured presence, had to escort his Mother according to the flesh, truly all-blessed and happy, more excellent than all generations and the whole creation. All stood by her as she shone with the beacon-fire of the Spirit and with brilliant flashes lit up those who, with reverence and fear and unwavering longing, fixed on her the pure eye of the mind. For there is nothing among the things that are which is not of this nature, except the One alone: for by being beyond them it is none of the things that are, and, set beside nothing, it comes down, and indeed comes down to all, acting and not admitting of being acted upon.

choices.note: Exodus 20:12 is cited for 'the One who made it law to honour parents' (the commandment, not a quotation).
Matthew 4:19 and Luke 5:10 (fishing for men, catching men alive) and Matthew 22:2 (the king's wedding feast for his son) are clear allusions;
Luke 1:2 ('eyewitnesses and servants of the word') is cited from its wording though not in the print's margin.
Doubtful syntax: 'very most royally' (λίαν βασιλικώτατα) may go with the Father's feast or with the divine command; the English joins it to the feast.

The closing sentence ('For there is nothing among the things that are ...') is obscure: the PG editor's note says Billius omitted it, the codices have it, it is most obscure and fits poorly with what precedes, and the Seguerianus reads a shorter form; the column margin refers it to Dionysius, Divine Names 2.
The English follows the print clause by clause and does not smooth it into a clearer argument.
Apparatus: ἐπιφανοῦς (R. 2, Colb., Germ. add 'from heaven', already present in the next clause);
'The foremost' renders ἀκρέμονας, literally 'the topmost branches'.

'Word' is capitalised in 'servants of the Word' because the next clause calls her 'his mother' (τῇ τούτου μητρί, referring to τοῦ λόγου); the facing Latin reads the same way ('ministri verbi ... ipsius etiam matri').
The facing Latin also joins 'most royally' to the Father's feast ('magnifice et regie admodum celebrat'), as the English does.
For the obscure closing sentence the facing Latin translates a different text (no order of heaven was absent and none refused to come down); the English follows the Greek print.

Unprinted allusions: Matt 4:19 / Luke 5:10 (fishing for men), Matt 22:2 (the wedding feast), Exod 20:12 (honouring parents, behind τοῦ γεραίρειν τοὺς τεκόντας θεσμοθετήσαντος).
